claims.text: The initial catalyst is a nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution.
The as-synthesized catalyst is a homogeneous alloy.
Controlled potential cycling at low anodic potentials can selectively enrich Ru or Rh at the catalyst surface.
Low-temperature annealing under a mildly oxidizing atmosphere can selectively enrich Ru or Rh at the catalyst surface.
Surface enrichment of Ru or Rh alters local intermetallic bonding.
Surface enrichment of Ru or Rh alters the surface electronic structure.
The altered surface electronic structure reduces the dissolution kinetics of surface-enriched Ru or Rh during oxidative potential cycling.
Reduced metal dissolution enhances catalyst durability during ethanol oxidation.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the pre-treated catalyst will lose catalytic activity more slowly during long-term testing.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the pre-treated catalyst will undergo material dissolution more slowly.
The pre-treated catalyst will have a measurably higher surface concentration of Ru or Rh.
The appropriate baseline is the untreated, as-synthesized PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst.
The proposed durability effect is expected to hold in acidic electrolyte under ethanol-oxidation potential cycling.
The proposed effect is expected to hold between 25 °C and 80 °C.
The magnitude of the durability enhancement and the optimal pre-treatment conditions are not yet known.
Elements other than Ru and Rh may contribute to the durability response.
A statistically significant difference in degradation rate or surface Ru/Rh enrichment can be assessed by comparing pre-treated and untreated catalysts under otherwise identical conditions.
